title: Autopsy and Witness
premise: Estate lawyer Isandro Thackeray is summoned to read the will of Judge Aurelio Vance, a man officially dead for twelve years — and the will names her as executor of a sealed case file she herself archived. Twin letters arrive: one confessing to the unsolved drowning of a girl named Marisol, one promising that 'the rest' will follow unless Isandro finds who among the town's founding families has been editing the record all along. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Isandro realizes the killer has been feeding her curated memories, using her own meticulous filing system as both weapon and alibi. In the climax she stages a false reading of the will's codicil at the county courthouse, forcing the killer — the judge's surviving twin brother, who has impersonated the dead man for years — to destroy the file in front of witnesses; the confession letter was written by Marisol's sister, who spent twelve years becoming Isandro's clerk to place it in her hands.
about_author: Yara Villalobos is a former probate paralegal from the Rio Grande Valley who spent a decade handling estates with more secrets than assets. She writes mysteries about paper trails and the people they bury.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro Thackeray opens a probate appointment expecting routine business and instead reads the will of Judge Aurelio Vance — dead twelve years, or so every record she filed says. The document names her executor of a sealed annex. POV: Isandro. Beat: cold dread dressed as professional composure.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Two envelopes arrive the same morning: one confessing to Marisol Reyes's 2012 drowning in precise legal language, one promising 'the rest' if Isandro follows the annex's instructions. She recognizes the typewriter font from old court filings. POV: Isandro. Beat: the past knocking with excellent penmanship.

chapters.title: The Alphabetized Town
chapters.summary: Isandro walks the reader through Halcón Bend's founding families and how her firm keeps their sins filed cross-referenced and quiet. Her clerk, Dolores, watches her too closely. POV: Isandro. Beat: complicity examined — she built the machine now aimed at her.

chapters.title: Exhumation Denied
chapters.summary: Isandro petitions to verify Vance's death; the county clerk produces a burial permit signed by a coroner who retired before the date on it. Someone anticipated this move years ago. POV: Isandro. Beat: first proof the conspiracy predates her involvement.

chapters.title: Marisol, Age Seventeen
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the summer of 2012, told through Isandro's memory of the case she helped close as a junior associate — an accidental drowning, a grieving family, a settlement nobody asked for. POV: Isandro. Beat: guilt surfacing like something floated up from the river.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Filed Papers
chapters.summary: Dolores reveals fragments of her past; Isandro discovers her clerk's employment history has gaps matching the years after Marisol's death. She says nothing, testing what Dolores knows. POV: Isandro. Beat: suspicion turning inward on the one person she trusts.

chapters.title: A Visit from the Living Dead
chapters.summary: A man identifying himself as Aurelio Vance appears at Isandro's office, alive, courteous, and asking her to withdraw the petition. His hands shake when she mentions his late wife. POV: Isandro. Beat: uncanny terror — the dead man is warm, breathing, and lying.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Following the will's instructions, Isandro opens the sealed annex: twelve years of surveillance photos, financial ledgers, and a list of payments from four founding families to someone labeled only 'W.' POV: Isandro. Beat: vertigo of scale — this was never one crime.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro interviews Marisol's mother, who produces a letter Marisol mailed the day she died, describing being followed by a man who smelled of the courthouse basement. POV: alternating Isandro and the mother's account. Beat: grief as evidence.

chapters.title: Edited Memory
chapters.summary: Isandro pulls her own archived files and finds pages subtly altered — dates shifted, initials swapped — edits only someone with her filing key could make. The killer knows her system intimately. POV: Isandro. Beat: paranoia; her life's work turned against her.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: With nineteen days until the homicide clock expires, Isandro maps the deadline against the will's conditions and realizes the annex was designed to be opened exactly now — timed by someone who knew probate procedure cold. POV: Isandro. Beat: the trap has a schedule.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Daughter
chapters.summary: Tracking the impossible burial permit, Isandro finds the retired coroner's daughter, who admits her father falsified the death certificate under threat — and left a sealed statement naming who threatened him. POV: Isandro. Beat: a door opening onto the real architecture of power.

chapters.title: Payment Due
chapters.summary: One of the four families, the Okonkwos, tries to buy Isandro off with a partnership offer; their patriarch lets slip that 'W' stopped cashing checks three years ago. Whoever W was, they're dead or transformed. POV: Isandro. Beat: corruption offering a comfortable exit.

chapters.title: Dolores Confesses (Partially)
chapters.summary: Dolores admits she is Marisol's sister and that she wrote the second letter — but swears the first confession letter isn't hers. She came to watch Isandro either break the case or bury it again. POV: Dolores. Beat: betrayal braided with alliance.

chapters.title: The Impostor Problem
chapters.summary: Comparing the living 'Vance' against archival records, Isandro confirms he is Aurelio's twin, Emilio, presumed drowned as a boy — meaning the real judge may have died twelve years ago after all, and someone profited from the swap. POV: Isandro. Beat: the mystery inverts; identity itself is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the timeline, Isandro finds Emilio killed Aurelio over the family's blackmail ledger, assumed his identity, and used the town's reverence for the judge as armor. Marisol saw him dispose of evidence. POV: Isandro. Beat: clarity arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: The File That Fights Back
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into Isandro's office and reorders her entire archive alphabetically wrong — a message: we can unmake everything you've built. A threatening note cites a detail only the true killer would know. POV: Isandro. Beat: fear made personal and procedural.

chapters.title: Setting the Codicil
chapters.summary: Isandro drafts a fake codicil announcing the annex's public unsealing at a special probate session, and leaks word through exactly the channels Emilio monitors. Dolores helps, knowing it may be bait for them both. POV: Isandro. Beat: the hunted choosing to become the trapper.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Later
chapters.summary: At the packed courthouse reading, Emilio comes to destroy the annex personally, producing a gun when the codicil proves genuine-looking enough. He confesses aloud, certain no record will survive him. POV: Isandro. Beat: climax — the killer defeated by his own need to control the file.

chapters.title: Witness for the Prosecution
chapters.summary: The sheriff's hidden recorder, planted via Dolores, captures everything; Emilio is arrested as the statute expires at midnight. The four families begin turning on each other within the week. POV: Isandro. Beat: catharsis — paper finally cutting the powerful.

chapters.title: Probate Closed
chapters.summary: Isandro settles the estate honestly for the first time in her career, restoring Marisol's name to the record and giving Dolores the original confession letter to do with as she wishes. POV: Isandro. Beat: inheritance redefined — what we leave behind versus what we take.

chapters.title: Alphabetical Order Restored
chapters.summary: Months later, Isandro refiles her archive, leaving deliberate gaps where secrets used to live. A new letter arrives — unsigned, promising nothing — and she smiles, files it, and locks the drawer. POV: Isandro. Beat: quiet, earned peace with one honest ambiguity.
